calendar.title: The fire calendar
calendar.intro: Each row is a year, each square a week. Colour shows harmonised fire activity on the VIIRS scale, so every year can be compared.
calendar.highlight: Click a year to highlight it
calendar.keyboard: Use arrow keys to move between weeks and years.

sensors.title: Why harmonise?
sensors.intro: Two NASA instruments watch the same fires but count them differently. If you join their records where VIIRS begins, fire appears to quadruple overnight in 2012.
sensors.ratioTitle: VIIRS sees more, and how much more depends on the month
sensors.ratioIntro: VIIRS / MODIS detections by month, 2012 to 2024. One conversion factor cannot fit both the spring peak and the small winter fires.
sensors.validationTitle: Tested on years the model never saw
sensors.validationIntro: Leave one year out, 2012 to 2024: fit on 12 years, predict the 13th from MODIS only, and compare with what VIIRS really saw.
sensors.case2022: The 2022 test: MODIS says fire fell 67% from 2021, VIIRS says 41%. With 2022 held out, the single factor predicts {{naive}} detections, our model {{pred}}, and VIIRS observed {{true}}. Hard years remain hard; the model narrows the gap but does not close it.
sensors.bridgeIntro: Suomi NPP stops sending data on {{date}}. NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 carry the same VIIRS instrument. Over {{from}} to {{to}} NOAA-20 counted {{n20}} detections against {{snpp}} for S-NPP, a {{diff}}% difference, so the record continues on NOAA-20/21 with monthly factors near 1.
sensors.withKilns: Include brick kilns and other fixed heat sources (unfiltered record)

map.colour: District colour: season so far vs normal

method.title: Method and data
method.intro: How the record was built, how well it works, and how to reuse it.
method.limitsText: Values for 2003 to 2011 are estimates with 80% intervals, not observations. Weeks where MODIS saw nothing cannot reveal how many small fires VIIRS would have seen; the band shows that. The app describes fire detected; it does not forecast individual fires, monitor the Sundarbans, or link hill fires to Dhaka's winter smoke.

outlook.title: Early warning
outlook.intro: Where fire is likely to run above normal in the next two weeks, how dangerous the weather is for fire, and which districts are unusually active right now.
outlook.normalIs: Normal for these two weeks: about {{n}}
outlook.quiet: Quiet time of year: too little fire for an outlook to mean much.
outlook.dangerIntro: Canadian Fire Weather Index from NASA POWER weather, with the next 15 days from a weather forecast. The band is the normal range for the date.
outlook.alertsIntro: Districts where this week's fire is above the 90th percentile for the time of year (at least 5 detections).
outlook.noAlerts: No district has unusual fire activity in the last 8 weeks.
outlook.feedsIntro: Machine-readable feeds for agencies and newsrooms: RSS, and CAP (Common Alerting Protocol), the standard used by disaster-warning systems.
outlook.seasonNoSkill: Tested on 23 past seasons, no method beat the normal range for the season total, so we show the normal instead of a guess.
outlook.seasonNormal: A normal January–May season here: {{lo}} to {{hi}} detections (median {{mid}}).
outlook.skillIntro: Tested on 2003–2025, one year held out at a time. Skill is measured against simply assuming a normal fortnight.
outlook.reliability: When we say X%, it happens about X% of the time
outlook.driverFire: Fire in the last 4 weeks: {{r}}× normal
outlook.driverFwi: Fire weather next 2 weeks: {{d}} vs normal
outlook.notForecast: Outlooks describe how much fire satellites are likely to detect in an area. They do not predict individual fires.

borders.title: Fire without borders
borders.intro: The same harmonised record, extended across the border: the hill fire season the Chittagong Hill Tracts share with Tripura, Mizoram and Chin State, and the crop burning upwind of Dhaka.
borders.hillsIntro: Fire detections per year on the VIIRS scale. MODIS years before 2012 are estimated with the same model, trained on each area's own overlap years.
borders.igpIntro: Weekly fire detections across the Indo-Gangetic Plain, and aerosol optical depth over Dhaka (NASA POWER). The Department of Environment can watch the upwind burning build before the haze arrives.
borders.caution: We do not claim that one causes the other: haze in Dhaka has many sources. The chart shows timing only.

method2.partnerIntro: ESA's Fire_cci burned-area maps (Sentinel-3 SYN and the harmonised medium-resolution product) come from changes in surface reflectance, not from thermal hotspots. They are an independent witness of the same fire seasons.
method2.jump: Change at the 2012 sensor switch, relative to burned area
method2.coverageText: Our 80% bands are built from errors on held-out years. Checked the same way, they contained the truth in {{w}}% of weeks and {{y}}% of years.
method2.bridgeText: NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 carry the same VIIRS instrument. On held-out years, applying no correction beat every fitted factor (season-total error {{e20}}% for NOAA-20, {{e21}}% for NOAA-21), so the record continues on their average without adjustment.
method2.fwiText: The Fire Weather Index uses daily maximum temperature, mean humidity, 10 m wind and rain. Noon humidity is lower than the daily mean, so absolute values run a little low; we use anomalies against each date's normal.

local.note: Upazila and union calendars: VIIRS detections from 2012; before 2012 the district estimate is shared by where MODIS saw fire. Small areas have few fires, so read the pattern, not single squares. Union names are in English only for now.
